title.en: Authored locomotion with visible stance and swing

summary: Coordinate root travel and limb motion so a creature communicates intended contact without pretending to solve biomechanics.
objective: Track a stance foot against a ground marker; unintended sliding is visible and can be corrected.
example_prompts: Coordinate root travel and limb motion so a creature communicates intended contact without pretending to solve biomechanics.

principles: Classify prescribed walking as kinematics. A believable gait can be authored without claiming force balance or muscle simulation.
Choose a contact schedule first: identify stance feet, swing feet and the intended support surface at each part of the cycle.
implementation: Keep canonical root position and gait phase. Derive limb targets from phase and route distance rather than unrelated sine loops.
During stance, preserve the selected foot target in world space; during swing, use an authored clearance arc. Handle turns by updating future placements.
Give route speed zero a clear idle pose; do not keep stepping while the creature is paused.
observable_checks: Track a stance foot against a ground marker; unintended sliding is visible and can be corrected.
Slow playback shows a lifted swing foot and continuous attachment at the joints.
Stop, reverse or reset the route without a one-frame limb jump or accumulated phase drift.

known_limits: Foot locking is a presentation constraint; it does not establish traction, stability, collision avoidance or dynamic balance.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt proportions, finish and presentation to the scene; explain deliberate departures from this guidance.
